title: England Beat India by 27 Runs at Lord's to Win ODI Series 2-1
excerpt: Ben Duckett's record-breaking 141 and Sam Curran's four wickets sealed England's first bilateral ODI series win over India since 2018, despite Rohit Sharma's historic century.
body:
• England won the third ODI by 27 runs at Lord's, taking the series 2-1 — their first bilateral ODI series victory over India since 2018.
  • Ben Duckett hit 141 off 135 balls, the highest individual ODI score at Lord's, surpassing Viv Richards's 138 not out from the 1979 World Cup final.
  • Rohit Sharma scored 138 off 110 balls — the first Indian to hit an ODI century at Lord's — but India collapsed after his dismissal.
  • India's white-ball tour ends in disappointment, having lost T20 series to both Ireland and England before falling in the ODIs.

Duckett Rewrites the Record Books

Ben Duckett put on a batting masterclass at the Home of Cricket, smashing 141 from 135 balls to set the tone for England's mammoth 387-3. His innings, featuring 18 fours and a six, eclipsed Viv Richards's legendary 138 not out in the 1979 World Cup final as the highest individual ODI score at Lord's.

Duckett shared a 192-run opening stand with Jacob Bethell, who contributed 91 — England's highest opening partnership against India in ODI cricket. From that platform, Joe Root added an unbeaten 74, his sixth consecutive ODI half-century, while Jos Buttler blasted 41 not out off just 13 balls to propel England past the 350 mark.

"Rohit Sharma delivered, sharing a 147-run opening stand with Shubman Gill and powering to 138 off 110 balls."

"Rohit Sharma delivered, sharing a 147-run opening stand with Shubman Gill and powering to 138 off 110 balls."

The total of 387-3 was England's highest at Lord's in ODIs, shattering their own 51-year-old record of 334-4 set against India at the same ground in 1975.

Rohit's Heroics Fall Short

Facing a daunting target of 388, India needed something special. Rohit Sharma delivered, sharing a 147-run opening stand with Shubman Gill and powering to 138 off 110 balls. At 39, he became the oldest centurion at Lord's and the first Indian to score an ODI hundred at the iconic venue — surpassing Sourav Ganguly's 90 from 2004.

"Rohit Sharma's 34th ODI hundred was a thrilling reminder of his continuing value, but the middle order's collapse underlined the gulf between captain and crew."

— Match Analysis

But once Bethell's slow left-arm spin dismissed Rohit, the chase unraveled. Sam Curran ripped through the middle order with 4-75, taking three wickets in seven deliveries. India, who were cruising at one stage, fell further behind the required rate and were eventually bowled out 27 runs short.

A Disappointing Tour for India

The series loss caps a miserable white-ball trip for India. Shreyas Iyer's side lost the T20 series 2-0 to Ireland before falling 2-1 to England in the T20Is. The ODI series defeat makes it a clean sweep of losses across formats.

India's bowling attack, missing the injured Jasprit Bumrah, struggled throughout the decider. Gurnoor Brar conceded 97 runs in his 10 overs — the most expensive figures by an Indian bowler against England in ODIs — while Prince Yadav's 1-79 included seven wides.

What's Next

For India, the immediate focus shifts to evaluating squad composition ahead of the Champions Trophy later this year. Rohit's century at 39 argues powerfully for his continued inclusion, but the team's inability to defend or chase totals consistently raises broader concerns about pace-bowling depth and middle-order reliability. England, meanwhile, will take confidence from a series victory that suggests their white-ball rebuild under head coach Marcus Trescothick is gaining traction.
